entries.testAndInterview:
Technical/HR test: 
●​ Difficulty Level: Moderate to high 
●​ Types of Questions: 
The technical test included core engineering questions based on 
Mechanical and Electrical concepts. 
Topics included fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, manufacturing, 
control systems, and power systems (particularly in the Electrical 
Engineering paper). 
The test required a good understanding of GATE-level problems and 
fundamentals across design, thermal, and manufacturing domains. 
●​ Structure: 
Candidates who cleared the technical test were moved to the 
personality (behavioral) test round. 
The personality test included situational and behavioral questions 
aimed at assessing honesty and decision-making ability. 
●​ Tips for Preparation: 
●​ Revise core concepts thoroughly and practice GATE-level problems 
under time constraints. 
●​ Focus on understanding basic principles and solving practical 
application-based problems. 
 
 Interviews 
●​ Number of Rounds: Two – one Technical and one HR 
●​ Mode: Online  
●​ Panel Structure: One main interviewer conducted the session, 
although two individuals were present in the meeting. 
●​ Difficulty Level: Moderate 
22 

 
●​ Technical Interview: 
Focused on resume details, particularly academic and 
project-related work. 
Emphasis on practical application and understanding of engineering 
principles behind project decisions, such as dimensions and the 
reasoning behind chosen approaches. 
If the resume aligned with the role, in-depth questions were asked on 
the projects; otherwise, focus was placed on core subject knowledge. 
HR Interview: 
Questions included general topics like relocation readiness, future 
academic plans, family background, and motivation for joining the 
company. 
Responses were expected to be honest and reflective of long-term 
interest. 
 
●​     Tips for Preparation: 
 
Be thorough with every detail mentioned in the resume. 
Understand technical concepts behind your projects and be ready to 
explain their implementation.
entries.jobDescription:
Role Overview:We are looking for fresh graduates with a strong foundation in 
Mechanical and Electrical Engineering to contribute to our Research and 
20 

 
Development (R&D). This role offers a unique opportunity to apply your 
problem-solving skills and technical knowledge to live projects and gain hands-on 
experience in a supportive environment. 
Key Responsibilities: 
●​ Research and Development: Assist in designing, testing, and optimizing new 
products and systems. Support ongoing R&D projects by conducting 
experiments, analyzing data, and contributing to innovative solutions. 
●​ Technical Analysis: Utilize your understanding of mechanical and electrical 
principles to analyze and solve complex problems. Provide technical insights 
and support for project development. 
●​ Market Understanding: Apply your knowledge of market trends and industry 
standards to inform project decisions and contribute to the development of 
competitive products. 
 
 
Qualifications: 
●​ Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical 
Engineering, or a related field. 
●​ Technical Knowledge: Strong foundational knowledge in mechanical and 
electrical principles. Familiarity with industry-standard tools and software is a 
plus. 
●​ Problem-Solving Skills: Demonstrated ability to analyze problems, develop 
solutions, and implement them effectively. 
●​ Market Awareness: Basic understanding of current market trends and industry 
practices relevant to engineering and technology. 
●​ Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills. Ability to 
work effectively in a team and present technical information clearly. 
●​ Enthusiasm: Eagerness to learn, adapt, and grow in a fast-paced environment.
entries.preparationMaterials:
Test preparation involves reviewing class notes, course PPTs, and previous year 
GATE questions to strengthen core subject understanding. For the interview, it is 
important to be thorough with the resume and projects, using resources like HR 64 
questions for common queries. A final review of the resume with peer input can also 
be helpful.
entries.suggestions:
Maintain a consistent preparation schedule, attend PPTs on time, and avoid taking on 
too many commitments during the semester. Practice aptitude daily, preferably in a 
group for better accountability. For core preparation, having a backup profile is 
advisable

entries.testAndInterview:
1) Technical/HR Tests: 
The technical test focused primarily on Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA), with 
around 2–3 questions of LeetCode Medium level. The duration was typically 90 
minutes. Preparing through platforms like NeetCode 150 and practicing core DSA 
30 

 
patterns can be very helpful. The difficulty was moderate, and a strong grasp of 
problem-solving approaches is essential. 
 
2) Case Study/Rounds: 
A system design-oriented case study was conducted, where candidates had to 
design a solution for handling transactions or demonstrate understanding of 
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles. Time allotted was around 1 hour. 
Understanding the practical application of data structures and having clarity on basic 
system design/OOP concepts helped in approaching this round. 
 
3) Interviews: 
There were three rounds of interviews, all conducted offline. 
 
Round 1: Focused on discussing the case study solution, exploring alternate 
approaches and the logic behind the design. 
 
Round 2: Centered around previous industrial/internship experience, with in-depth 
questions about projects undertaken. 
 
Round 3 (HR): Involved situational and behavioral questions to assess your approach 
to hypothetical scenarios. 
The interviewers were friendly, supportive, and open to discussion. Overall difficulty 
was manageable for those well-prepared. It helps to be confident with your projects 
and comfortable articulating your thought process.

important, so practicing more problems is beneficial.

advanced profit-loss concepts. These can be solved once you understand the 
questions. No specific preparation was needed for the technical part.​

Duration: Around 45 minutes​
Content: 2-3 questions based on statistics, guesstimates, and a case to solve.​
Approach: Statistics questions were straightforward. Sharing your structured 
thoughts with the interviewer is very helpful. The final answer is of secondary 
importance. 
​
Second Round:​
Duration: Around an hour​
Content: 3 different product case-solving questions. It was an interactive interview, 
and the cases were difficult.​
Approach: Show the interviewer your structured way of thinking and ask questions if

entries.suggestions:
The student said that one should start as soon as possible and also it's never too late 
to start. It depends on the student's internship; some may have high chances of 
getting a PPO (Pre-Placement Offer) so they need not prepare much until the 
internship gets over. If the student is not interested in continuing in that industry, 
Semester 6 would be a good time to start preparing. 
 
1.​ Resume Formatting: The student said that he asked some seniors and took 
their resume for preparing his own resume. He started preparing one week 
before the deadline and added that it is wrong to start preparing the resume 
this late. The time taken to prepare the resume may vary from person to 
person; some people may have projects and their previous resumes from the 
internship season, so they may take less time to prepare their resumes. He 
checked his resume score using AI-powered score checkers available online, 
which provided the ATS (Applicant Tracking System) score points. He spent 
around 2 to 3 days on the resume since he had already prepared one for the 
internship and just wanted to 
add more things to it. He prepared it on his own. 
2.​ Other specific things related to the process: If you are preparing for a software 
development profile, it is important to solve new questions. It's not necessary 
to solve a large number of questions. Solving new questions is more important 
than solving a large number of questions because if an entirely different 
question comes in the exam, your approach matters. Practicing solving new 
questions is crucial. The GD conducted by this firm was quite interesting, 
unlike other CS firms.​

entries.testAndInterview:
1. Technical Test:​
• Content: 2 DSA questions (simple or standard)​
• Preparation Tip: Solve Striver’s DSA sheet (200 questions) to handle both 
questions in 10-15 minutes.​
• Selection Criteria: Speed is crucial; some were not shortlisted despite solving both 
questions due to slower speed.​
111 

 
• Difficulty: Easy to medium​
• Duration: 1 hour​
• Topics: Basic Python (lists, sorting, maps, dictionaries, sort functions)​
​
2. Interviews:​
• Mode: Fully offline, face-to-face​
• Rounds: 3​
    1) Round 1: Technical - DSA Problem Solving​
        • Format: Solve DSA questions on paper, explain, and write the code.​
        • Questions: Sliding Window (easy), Recursion​
        • Experience: Solved the first question in 18-20 minutes with 3 methods.​
    2) Round 2: Technical and Project Discussion​
        • Interviewer: Director of Software Development​
        • Content: Discussion about job role, tech stacks, and current projects. ​
    3) Round 3: HR Round​
        • Questions: Introduction, reasons for choosing JPMC and the role, preference for     
JPMC, innovative problem-solving experiences. 
    4) Round 1: Technical (Additional Details)​
       • Content: Finding whether a directed graph has a cycle or not (easy).​
    5) Round 2: Technical (Additional Details)​
       • Interviewer: French interviewer​
       • Content: Algorithm discussion, DBMS-related questions (moderate/tricky).​
      6) Round 3: HR (Additional Details)​
         • Content: Job-specific description/details, reasons for choosing JPMC.​
      7) Overall Interview Difficulty: Easy to moderate​
      8) Panelists: 3-4 (varied by round)​
​
3. General Tips:​
• Technical Test: Focus on basic DSA and Python fundamentals.​
• Interviews: Be prepared for both DSA problem-solving and project discussions. Be 
confident, and know your resume well.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. has expanded its consumer business and we have launched a 
new digital retail bank in the UK and we're busy planning our next phase of growth, 
including developing new products and expanding to new countries – so it's an 
incredibly exciting time to jump on board. We are offering consumers a completely 
new banking experience. Under the Chase brand, the bank provides products and 
109 

 
features tailored to meet the needs of customers in the UK, made available via an 
innovative mobile app. Our team is at the heart of building this new venture, focused 
on developing offerings that put the customer at the center. We have created a new 
organization and we are looking for solution oriented, commercially minded, 
customer-focused engineers, used to working in a true agile environment who want 
to be a part of something new, built from the ground up as a greenfield with zero 
legacy initiative within a global, diverse and inclusive team. Culture is as important to 
us and we are looking for intellectually curious, new technology passionate 
individuals who would like to expand their skills whilst working on a new exciting 
venture for the firm. Your work will have a direct impact to our customers as our 
business expands around the world. What to expect: The SGEP gives you the tools 
and experience you need to become a skilled software engineer, by empowering you 
to harness insights and help us build innovative customer experiences in a fulltime, 
18 month program. You’ll start with an in-depth orientation covering our strategies, 
products and systems, as well as an overview of our technology community and 
what it takes to get genius ideas into the hands of our customers. You'll work with 
teams across lots of different areas of the business, and have access to a huge range 
of skillsets, leadership styles and opportunities to learn from technologists all over 
the world. Through this new-found network, we'll help you evolve your professional 
skills with mentorship, training and plenty of hands-on experience. On a more 
personal level, you'll also spend time learning from your peers as you support each 
other to grow. This is a hands-on role for a software engineer who wants to be part 
of an organization with a flat-structure. You’ll be responsible for delivering 
end-to-end cutting-edge solutions leveraging the latest cloud-native technologies 
(Kubernetes/Istio, GraphQL, React Native, Cockroach, Kafka) and the best industry 
practices. About You: We understand that everyone's unique – and that diversity of 
thought, experience and backgrounds is what makes a good team, great. By bringing 
people with different points of view together, we can represent everyone and truly 
reflect the communities we serve. Your technical skills should include: • 
Qualifications in computer science or STEM related field (science, technology, 
engineering or mathematics) or foreign equivalent • Exposure to a professional 
experience working in an agile, dynamic and customer facing environment • Solid 
Computer Science fundamentals • Sound knowledge of software architectural 
patterns and development processes • Ability to code in a High-level programming 
language (Java/Python/Javascript (preferably Java 8+ )) • Desired – basic 
110 

 
understanding of distributed systems and microservices architecture • Desired – 
basic understanding of RESTful APIs and web technologies • Desired – basic 
understanding of relational databases • Desired – basic understanding of public 
cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, etc.) • Desired – understanding of dependency 
injection frameworks • Desired – basic understanding of containers (Docker, 
Kubernetes, Helm, etc.) • Desired – basic understanding of automating deployment, 
releases and testing in continuous integration, continuous delivery pipelines • 
Desired – basic understanding to writing unit level tests using mocking frameworks, 
as well as automating component, integration and end-to-end tests Your soft skills 
should include: • Ability to work in a dynamic, collaborative, agile environment within 
a geographically distributed team • Ability to focus on promptly addressing customer 
needs • Ability to work within a diverse and inclusive team • Technically curious, 
eager to learn, versatile and solution oriented • Excellent written and verbal 
communication skills in English

entries.shortlistingProcess:
Candidates were shortlisted through an aptitude test, 
followed by a case-based problem-solving round and multiple technical and 
HR interviews.
entries.testAndInterview:
The selection process began with a 1-hour aptitude test covering quantitative 
aptitude, logical reasoning, and grammar. Once shortlisted, candidates entered 
a case study/problem-solving round, where concepts were explained over 30 
minutes, followed by three questions requiring graph-based, analytical 
responses. This round was conducted on pen and paper. 
Subsequently, five interview rounds were held, each being 
elimination-based: 
●​ Round 1: Candidates explained the solutions from the case study round, 
showcasing their understanding and reasoning. 
●​ Round 2: The interviewer provided reading material and then asked 
candidates to explain their approach to a new problem set, testing 
self-learning and interpretation.​
Round 3: A casual discussion with a US-based interviewer focused on 
the candidate’s background and exposure, while also sharing insights 
into KLA’s work culture and goals. 
●​ Round 4: A highly technical round, where another US-based interviewer 
deeply analyzed the candidate’s PhD project, probing the level of depth, 
clarity, and originality. 
●​ Round 5 (HR): Evaluated the candidate’s mindset, adaptability, and 
readiness to work in a fast-paced and demanding environment, 
emphasizing personality fit and soft skills.​
125 

 
The overall process tested technical competency, research depth, 
real-world application, and communication skills.

• For HR interviews, give opinionated answers and answer clearly with YES/NO. 
Avoid using words like "maybe" or "can be" in interviews.​
• Be consistent with the types of answers you give for personality tests. Ensure 
similar questions receive the same type of answer to maintain a high score in 
personality tests.​
• In GDs, expect situation-based questions such as leading a team or managing a 
plant during a critical task.​
• Discuss past experiences, internships, or projects where you demonstrated relevant 
skills during GDs. Speak naturally and confidently.​
• Common HR interview questions include your motivation to join the company, 
details about your summer internships, reasons for not choosing consulting or not 
receiving a PPO, and your interest in FMCGs or other sectors.​
• GDs typically consist of one round and last about 45 minutes with 3 panelists.​
• Interviews usually involve two rounds, with each round lasting 25-30 minutes and 
conducted by one panelist.​

entries.suggestions:
• Start Early: Preparation for placements should ideally begin 2-3 months prior to the 
placement season, around June or July. For example, preparation for P&G placements 
was started in mid-September.​
• Contacting Seniors: Reach out to at least 4-5 seniors who have profiles similar to 
yours. This can be very helpful as they can provide insights and guidance based on 
their experiences.​
• Leverage PORs: Use Positions of Responsibility (PORs) to build connections. 
Seniors who are placed in FMCG companies can offer valuable advice. Contact those 
seniors who have given detailed video explanations or fundaes.​
• Resume Preparation: Start working on your resume early. Expect to make 30-40 
iterations. Ideally, it should take about 3 days to format it if all information is ready, 
but it can take up to a week.​
• Be Confident with Your Resume: Ensure your resume is well-prepared and you are 
confident in presenting it. This is crucial for making a strong impression.​
• HR Interviews: Google common HR interview questions for the company you are 
applying to. Sometimes, the same questions are asked in the interview.​
• Group Discussions (GD): Typically, 3 students are allotted for a GD slot, and the 
same questions will be asked one-to-one. For example, you might be asked to solve 
a conflict that arose in your team using your POR and intern skills.​
• Expect Competition: The competition is usually decent, with more people being 
shortlisted for GDs. However, the number of people interviewed will be fewer.​

Candidates were shortlisted based on a 3-hour 
take-home assignment, their resume, and a written essay on “Why do you 
want to join Sarvam?”.
entries.testAndInterview:
The process began with a 3-hour assignment round, where candidates had to 
develop a functional application leveraging LLMs. Creativity was encouraged 
169 

 
— ideas included image interpretation apps or multilingual voice translators 
using Sarvam’s own models. 
Post shortlisting, four interviews followed: 
●​ Round 1 & 2: Both were deep dives into the candidate’s resume, 
projects, and internships. System design questions were asked, such as 
“How would you build reliable automated agents for the hospitality 
industry?” or “How would you design Instagram’s content moderation 
system?” Candidates were expected to discuss ML/AI-based solutions at 
a high level. There was also a detailed discussion on the assignment 
submission, including tech stack choices, latency vs. correctness 
trade-offs, and database design. Each of these rounds lasted around 50 
minutes.​
 
●​ Round 3: A short 15-minute round focused on the candidate’s long-term 
interests, career goals, and alignment with Sarvam’s vision.​
 
●​ Round 4: Another technical round where the interviewer asked the 
candidate to pick a project and explain it thoroughly. This included 
technical decisions, challenges, and innovations — such as concurrency 
and parallel programming. The discussion also touched upon research 
experience and lasted around 15–20 minutes.​
 
Notably, there were no DSA-based questions. The company 
emphasized deep technical understanding and a broad 
systems-level view. Being a growing startup, the selection process 
may evolve in the future.

●​ Interview with 4 rounds( 3 technical , 1 techno-managerial)
entries.testAndInterview:
1. Technical/HR Tests:​
 The technical test was 1 hour long and conducted on the HackerRank platform. It 
consisted of 3 questions, all of which were follow-up problems based on the same 
core topic. Stripe does not ask traditional Leetcode-style DSA questions. For 
example, a sample question involved parsing an indefinite stream of strings in the 
format: "customerName, customerId, cardType, transactionDate, 
transactionAmount", and computing the total transaction amount for a specific 
customer using a specific card type on a given date. These are implementation-based 
problems and require attention to detail. Proper variable naming, code commenting, 
and overall code quality are crucial. It is not necessary to solve all questions or pass 
all test cases to be selected. Focus on code quality and try to complete at least one 
question entirely. 
2. Interviews:​
 There were a total of 4 interview rounds conducted online — 3 technical interviews 
(each of 1 hour) and 1 techno-managerial interview (30 minutes). Each round had a 
single panelist. Candidates were allowed to refer to online resources (such as 
GeeksforGeeks, StackOverflow, etc.) during the interview, provided they clearly 
communicated what they intended to search and why. Usage of LLMs was not 
180 

 
permitted. The programming language choice had to be shared in advance, and the 
panelist was assigned accordingly. 
●​ First Technical Round:​
 This round was similar in format to the online assessment. It involved 
implementation-based, string-parsing questions, with three follow-up 
problems from a single topic. This round was held in November and was of an 
eliminating nature.​
 
●​ Second Technical Round:​
 This was an implementation-based problem involving encoding and decoding 
logic. A GitHub link was provided to pull the base source code. Based on the 
discussion with the interviewer, three questions were posed — each a 
follow-up of the previous.​
 
●​ Third Technical Round:​
 This was a bug-squashing round. A GitHub link was shared containing a 
buggy project. The candidate had to identify and fix the issues while 
communicating their approach. The process involved running the code, 
analyzing the error, identifying the failing function or API, and navigating the 
project structure. Clear communication at each step was expected.​
 
●​ Techno-Managerial Round:​
 This final round was a discussion with a manager about the projects and 
internships listed in the resume. The questions focused on the technical 
aspects of the projects.​
 
Those who cleared the first (eliminating) round progressed to the remaining three 
(non-eliminating) rounds, which were conducted consecutively on 1st December. The 
final result was declared cumulatively after all interviews were completed.​

181 

 
platforms were not particularly helpful for Stripe’s test format. Regular coding 
practice in any language you are comfortable with is sufficient. The key is to be quick 
in developing a working solution. 
For the interviews as well, standard coding practice and the ability to think and

entries.suggestions:
The Stripe interviews are not based on traditional Leetcode or Codeforces-style DSA 
questions. The problems are more implementation-oriented. Candidates are given a 
large, real-life scenario and are expected to develop and explain a working solution. 
The focus is not on optimization but on building correct and maintainable code. 
Typically, each round involves 3–4 subproblems to be solved within 1 hour. It is 
important to specify your preferred programming language well in advance, as 
panelists are scheduled accordingly. 
Advice for Stripe: Focus on constructing and clearly explaining a working solution, 
even if it is brute-force. Optimization is not the priority — correctness, clarity, and 
code quality matter more. 
Additionally, I found it very helpful to refer to the resumes of my seniors. This helped 
me understand what to include and how to phrase it effectively. One particularly 
useful tip was to quantify every statement in the resume, as it adds significant value 
and clarity.

entries.testAndInterview:
1) Technical/HR Tests:​
 The technical test was fast-paced and divided into two components: 
●​ Quantitative Puzzles:​
The questions, particularly those on probability, were subjective and had a 
strict time limit of 5 minutes each. It was challenging to solve them within the 
given time, and relying on solutions from the internet was not 
effective—candidates who used external sources did not advance despite 
solving all questions. Practicing from standard probability books and 
appearing for multiple placement tests was sufficient preparation if one could 
think quickly under pressure. 
●​ Coding:​
 Coding was compulsory in C++. Although the final code didn’t run due to 
minor bugs, the basic logic was correct, and the test was still cleared. This 
indicates that evaluators considered the quality and approach of the code, not 
just successful execution. 
Tips for Preparation: 
●​ Practice time-bound problem solving in both probability and coding. 
●​ Focus on logical reasoning and clear coding structure over just correct outputs. 
●​ Attempt as many mock tests as possible to build speed and accuracy. 
2) Interviews:​
204 

 
 There were 4 technical interview rounds, each lasting 1 hour, conducted online due 
to a cyclone (originally planned to be offline). Each round had a different interviewer. 
●​ Round 1:​
 Focused on standard Brainstellar-style probability questions. Emphasis was 
placed on rigorous proofs over intuitive answers. For example, one had to 
prove why placing one red ball in one bin and the remaining balls in another 
maximizes the probability of drawing a red ball. 
●​ Round 2:​
 Covered less standard probability problems involving concepts like Catalan 
numbers. The interviewer was helpful, even when the candidate was stuck. 
●​ Round 3:​
 Focused entirely on the resume. Detailed questions were asked about 
internship experiences, research papers, and course projects. The interviewer 
also explored deep learning topics, including problem-solving puzzles (e.g., a 
variation of the Trexquant Hangman puzzle), and went into technical depth on 
architectures like Transformers, LSTMs, and RNNs. 
●​ Round 4:​
 Involved a single complex question combining Bayesian estimation and 
calculus. The problem required developing a strategy for determining the best 
coin to toss among N coins, each with an unknown probability of heads, using 
results from previous tosses. 
Overall Tips for Interviews: 
●​ Be well-prepared in probability, both standard and advanced topics. 
●​ Have a deep understanding of your resume, including internships, projects, 
and research. 
●​ Revise core concepts in deep learning and Bayesian methods. 
●​ Practice solving puzzles that require mathematical reasoning and 
model-building.

entries.testAndInterview:
1) Technical/HR Tests  
277 

 
● Format & Difficulty: One online assessment (mandatory for all profiles), with a 
cutoff around 300+ marks for the Product Analyst (PA) profile.  
● Type of Questions: Included mathematical puzzles, logical reasoning, basic 
programming (DSA), and product-based aptitude questions.  
● Duration: Around 60–90 minutes. 
2) Case Study / Rounds  
● Format & Difficulty: Moderate  
○ Round 1: Puzzle and Guesstimate (Moderate)  
○ Round 2: Deep Root Cause Analysis + DSA (Moderate to High) 
 ○ Round 3: Business Case Study with product development-oriented 
questions (Moderate)  
4) Interviews  
● Format: Total of 4 rounds, conducted online, starting around 5 PM and lasting till 
2 AM.  
● Panel: Mostly 1–2 panelists per round; the final HR round was taken by the 
Head of Business and Tech.  
● Difficulty:  
○ Round 1: Puzzles & Guesstimates – Moderate  
○ Round 2: DSA & RCA – Moderate to High  
○ Round 3: Product Case Study – Moderate  
○ Round 4 (HR): Easy, but very resume-specific  
● Tips: Be honest and thorough with everything you’ve written on your resume. The 
HR round focused deeply on extracurriculars and projects — the interviewer chose 
specific areas to go deeper into. Critical thinking and clarity of thought were key. 
Also, be prepared to talk about Inito’s work and your fit in the company in the short 
and long term.

The process began with resume shortlisting, followed by two technical 
interviews, both of which also included light HR components. 
●​ Round 1: A one-on-one conversation with the interviewer, where the 
resume was discussed in detail. The interviewer asked about past 
interviews, companies applied to, and previous experiences. The session 
was conversational, aiming to understand the candidate’s journey and 
interests. The interviewer also explained Lam’s work, followed by a few 
problem-solving questions to assess practical understanding.​
 
●​ Round 2: Conducted by two interviewers, this round was more exhaustive. 
It began with a resume deep-dive, followed by technical questions 
focused on core mechanical and thermal principles. Emphasis was placed 
on real-world applications, critical thinking, and analytical reasoning. 
Candidates were also asked to explain their projects and internship 
experiences. A few basic HR questions were sprinkled in to evaluate fit 
and mindset.

entries.testAndInterview:
Technical/HR Tests - The type of questions was mostly from the topics in Machine 
Learning, statistics and coding. As he had prepared for a long time, the tests did not 
seem very difficult to him. Some of the tips which he shared with me were: -  
A. The basic and popular codes and algorithms of Machine learning should be handy. 
B. Make proper use of online resources or any course you enrolled in for the topics like 
statistics, linear algebra, probability, machine learning and deep learning.  
C. If you are highly interested in mathematics, you have to be pretty strong in topics like 
statistics, linear algebra, and probability.  
301 

 
D. You must come up with proper logical answers during the tests. You must not deviate 
from the question asked in the test. You must give them practical solutions. Interviews - 
The interviews were not very difficult for him as he was well prepared for it. About the 
interviewer he said that he was very professional. He wanted sharp and to the point 
answers for his questions. He said that the interviewer should be slightly friendly, due 
to which he found him to be an average interviewer. There was only 1 guy in the panel.  
Some of the tips he suggested me were: -  
A. The interviewers don't really look at our spoken English. Just be confident with the 
words you are using. 
B. We should be very polite during the interview, and you should speak everything only 
to the point of the question he/she asked.  
C. Firstly, you should be clear on what you are speaking. You should clearly be able to 
explain your view on the question.  
D. Leave the question politely, if you don't know the proper answer. E. You must not 
argue with the interviewer at any point. You must sound polite every minute of the 
interview.  
E. If you feel your interview is going according to you, don't become overjoyed. You must 
be calm at all times. You must not act over smart in front of the interviewer. Always 
take time and think twice before answering any questions. He had 1 round of interviews 
and that too offline.

entries.preparationMaterials:
Resume preparation generally involves referring to previous years’ samples to 
understand effective formatting and relevant content. For coding tests, candidates 
typically practice competitive programming on platforms like Codeforces (targeting 
ratings around 1535) and complete structured resources such as the Striver DSA Sheet. 
DSA concepts are reinforced through GeeksforGeeks and LeetCode. After internships, 
the focus shifts to core computer science subjects—OOPs, Operating Systems, DBMS, 
and Computer Networks—using resources like GeeksforGeeks and curated online 
roadmaps. Interview preparation includes practicing common HR questions (such as 
self-introduction, strengths, and weaknesses), thoroughly reviewing the resume, and 
gathering insights from seniors’ interview experiences.
entries.suggestions:
To ensure a smooth placement experience, it is recommended to begin preparing at 
least two semesters in advance. Focus on strengthening core coding concepts such as 
Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) and Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs). 
Utilizing resources like Striver's DSA Sheet and thoroughly covering Computer Science 
fundamentals on platforms like GeeksforGeeks can be highly beneficial. 
323 

 
Additionally, don’t hesitate to reach out to seniors for guidance—they can offer 
valuable insights and help clear doubts. Building a supportive peer group is equally 
important. During interview days, having friends who can assist you, keep you 
motivated, and take care of small tasks will allow you to focus entirely on your 
performance.

The selection process comprised four in-person rounds, each approximately 90 minutes 
in duration. The focus was on a combination of core computer science fundamentals, 
AI/ML concepts, and practical application skills. 
●​ Round 1 – Technical Fundamentals & DSA​
 The first round covered fundamental data structures and algorithms, such as:​
 
○​ Finding the first k largest elements in an array​
374 

 
 
○​ Reversing a linked list in place​
 Additionally, candidates were asked to explain previous project 
experiences, particularly in computer vision and machine learning.​
 
●​ Round 2 – AI, NLP, and CV Concepts​
 This round assessed knowledge in deep learning, natural language processing, 
and computer vision, with questions on: 
○​ Architectural comparisons (e.g., ResNet vs VGG, GoogLeNet) 
○​ Attention mechanisms, LSTM and GRU structures 
○​ Concepts like Dropout, PCA, and regularization techniques​
 The emphasis was on conceptual clarity and technical depth.​
 
●​ Round 3 – Applied AI/ML Case Studies​
 Candidates were given real-world problem statements such as:​
 
○​ Improving drone landing accuracy using computer vision and sensor data 
○​ Designing a failure prediction model using time-series data from drone 
sensors​
 The evaluation focused on the approach, framework design, and selection 
of relevant techniques (e.g., LSTM, PCA, anomaly detection).​
 
●​ HR Round​
 The HR round focused on assessing the candidate’s fit with the company’s 
vision, workplace adaptability, and motivation for the role. It was conversational 
in nature. 
Tips 
●​ Prepare thoroughly on DSA, deep learning architectures, SQL, and core CS 
subjects 
●​ Practice designing solutions for applied AI problems and explaining them clearly

entries.testAndInterview:
1.​ Technical/HR Tests:​
 The technical assessment consisted of 20–24 MCQs covering topics such as 
SQL, probability, basic mathematics, pseudocode, and computer science 
fundamentals, along with 2 coding questions ranging from easy to hard 
(LeetCode medium-hard level). The test duration was 60–75 minutes and 
conducted online. MCQs were of moderate difficulty while the coding questions 
tested problem-solving and algorithmic skills.​
​
 Preparation Tips: Practice standard DSA problems from resources like Striver’s 
Sheet, LeetCode, GeeksforGeeks (GFG), Brainstellar, and CSES (selected 
problems).​
419 

 
 
2.​ Interviews:​
 There were three offline interview rounds: two technical and one HR.​
 
●​ Technical Round 1: Focused on resume-based questions, core CS fundamentals 
(DBMS, SQL vs NoSQL, indexing, OS concepts like paging and bootstrapping), 
Java (optional), threading, OOPs, and DSA questions on strings and arrays. 
Duration: 1–1.5 hours. 
●​ Technical Round 2: DSA-focused with questions from topics like graphs, trees, 
and permutations. Candidates were expected to write optimized solutions, 
including complete code with input handling, on paper. Duration: ~1 hour. 
●​ HR Round: Included behavioral and situational questions such as reasons for 
choosing Walmart, strengths, weaknesses, and overall college journey. Duration: 
15–20 minutes.​
 
Tips for Interviews:​
Stay confident, be honest about your skillset, and maintain a positive attitude even 
during challenging moments. Interviewers appreciate clarity of thought, structured 
problem-solving, and a calm demeanor.

Technical Tests: 
​
- Types of Questions: Covered basic machine learning concepts, Python programming, 
probability and statistics, SQL queries (including joins and group by), and general 
aptitude. 
- Time Duration: Typically 60–90 minutes 
- Preparation Tips: Focus on brushing up fundamental ML concepts, basic coding in 
Python, and core statistics/probability. Practice solving SQL queries on sample datasets 
and revise general aptitude questions from standard resources.​
 
Interviews: 
​
- Number of Rounds: Four technical rounds (three offline, one online with a VP) plus an 
HR round. 
- Interviewers: Usually a panel of 1–2 technical interviewers per round; the final round 
was with a VP. 
- Format: Combination of in-depth project discussion, data analysis exercises, 
ML/statistics questions, puzzles, and SQL questions. 
- Tips: Be clear in explaining your project experience, prepare logical explanations for 
all technical questions, and review probability/statistics basics. For the HR round, be 
yourself and clearly state your role preferences. 
- Mode: Mostly offline; the final interview round was online.​

entries.suggestions:
Start your DSA prep early with a solid and realistic plan. Solve 2–3 problems 
daily on platforms like LeetCode or InterviewBit. Don’t chase quantity — focus on 
quality problems that build depth in key areas. Explore CSES problem sets, 
especially for Graphs and DP.

explaining your code and approach clearly during interviews. Work on having at 
least a couple of good resume projects, and be ready to explain them in detail, 
especially the impact.

your achievements stand out. Participate in mock interviews and tests to 
simulate real situations. 
And most importantly — stay calm, stay consistent. If you face rejections, don’t 
get discouraged. Every interview adds experience. Keep improving, trust your 
prep, and believe in yourself.

Software engineering is one of five job families within Information Technology. Roles 
within this job family are responsible for  
●​ providing technical expertise in the development of business cases, analysis, 
workflows and requirements to implement or improve IT solutions.  
●​ development, testing, deploying, administering, configuring, operating, and 
supporting the lifecycle of software systems and environments.  
We are looking for motivated individuals to deliver innovative digital solutions through 
design, development, deployment, and support.  You will work on key projects and digital 
innovation initiatives following agile principals, collaborating with product teams to 
develop reusable software components and services.  
Successful candidates will develop digital solutions according to best practices and 
utilize standard tools to ensure quality and maintenance – excelling in modularity, 
scalability, observability, and integration.  This role provides opportunities to work across 
multiple areas, including web application development, system, and security 
design/development.  
Key responsibilities  
●​ Software Engineer 
●​ Hands-on coding to deliver functional, innovative software solutions.  
●​ Utilize CI/CD tooling to deploy software and iterate on solutions.  
●​ Design and develop data integration and data management practices and tools.  
●​ Maintain working knowledge of the latest tools and practices for continuous 
integration, unit tests, static and dynamic profiling, code coverage, code analysis, 
and automated tests.  
●​ Frequently work with global teams across time zones and provide support to 
application/solutions.   
●​ Application Engineering: 
●​ Hands-on development for integrating existing solutions with enterprise 
ecosystem (e.g., API development, Azure Data Factory)  
●​ Utilize CI/CD tooling to deploy software and iterate on solutions  
●​ Design and develop data integration and data management practices and tools  
●​ Understand technical requirements to maintain & support applications  
●​ Deploy, configure, support and enhance vendor software packages  
Experience  
506 

 
●​ Experience building solutions in one of the following: C#, C++, Angular, Node.js, 
SQL, Ansible, R, Java, Python  
●​ Strong familiarity with Gitflow and source control management methodologies  
●​ Experience with software development lifecycle (plan, design, develop, test, 
release, maintain and support, decommission) 
Preferred skills / competencies  
●​ Hands-on experience with Azure Cloud, Service Now, Ansible, and Azure DevOps  
●​ Experience working on agile teams, utilizing methodologies such as SAFe, Scrum, 
Kanban  
●​ Strong written and verbal communication  
●​ Demonstrated business negotiation skills, influence, conflict resolution, and 
resolving technical stalemates

entries.suggestions:
Start preparing at least a year in advance. Choose a primary and optionally a secondary 
domain, and avoid spending time on profiles unrelated to your interests. 
Stay consistent—prioritize progress over perfection—and regularly seek feedback from 
seniors. Build a healthy routine: eat well, exercise, and protect your health throughout 
the semester. Your well-being directly affects your performance. 
538 

 
Use the early part of the semester to plan other important activities, and stay updated 
with quizzes and endsems to avoid cramming later. Maintain support systems—lean on 
friends, stay in touch with family, and stay grounded. 
Take mock tests extensively during the summer and first two months, and shift focus to 
mock interviews in the final stretch. Accept that luck plays a role, and don’t dwell on 
setbacks—just keep moving forward. 
Above all, maintain integrity, give your best, and focus on what’s in your control.

583 

 
Education: M Tech – Chemical/Material Engineering 
 
Detailed job description: The candidate will be required to work in the R&T laboratory of Reliance 
New Energy – Battery division. His brief job responsibilities are given below 
 
1. Will need to make various design basis of new projects 
2. Will need to do 3D electrochemical calculation/simulation of battery materials 
3. Will need to do simulation of battery cell property using software like phyton, Ansys, GT Auto 
lion. 
4. Will need to do basic design of chemical reactors, sintering furnaces and air classification 
equipment 
5. Will need to understand and do powder processing 
6. Will need to do synthesis/production related to solid - liquid mixing/precipitation reactions in 
batch and continuous reactors with temperature variation, pH variability etc functions. 
7. Will need to do synthesis/production related with different wet/dry powder milling processes. 
8. Will need to do synthesis/production related to different liquid/solid separation processes. 
9. Will need to do synthesis/production related to different wet cake drying processes. 
10. Will need to do synthesis/production related to high temperature continuous calcination/inert 
atmosphere annealing processes. 
 
Experience and skills 
 
1. Should be a studious person 
2. Should be well versed with literature of various battery technologies 
3. Should be well versed with working in material synthesis laboratory 
4. Should be well versed with battery cell design 
5. Should be well versed with various slurry cast coating process used for battery cell 
6. Should be well versed with electrochemistry related to battery cell 
7. Should be well versed with principles of design basis in chemical engineering 
8. Should be well versed with various electrochemical simulation techniques like based on 
Phyton, Multiphysics based models etc 
9. Should be well versed with simulations of chemical engineering transport properties 
10. Should be well versed with mass transfer principles

1.​ Technical/HR Tests:​
 There was only one test round, which included both core technical and 
aptitude-based questions. The test duration was 2 hours, and the test window 
remained open for 24 hours. The difficulty level was moderate.​
 Tip: Prepare thoroughly on core subjects and practice aptitude questions 
regularly. Time management is key, so take a few full-length mock tests before 
the actual exam.​
​
 
2.​ Interviews:​
 A total of three interview rounds were conducted.​
 
●​ 1st Round:​
646 

 
 This was a mix of HR and technical questions. There were four panelists—one 
from HR and three from the technical team. The interview started with a 
question about why I wanted to join the company and where I see myself in five 
years. I was then asked to give a brief introduction, followed by a discussion on 
my M.Tech project. The panel also asked technical questions related to subjects 
like Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer.​
 
●​ 2nd Round:​
 This was a fully technical round with two new technical panelists. I explained 
my M.Tech project in detail, followed by related questions. They also asked about 
battery cooling technologies. Since my B.Tech project was also related to cooling 
systems, I discussed that as well. A conversation followed on improving battery 
cooling technology and how I could contribute to the company in that area.​
 
●​ 3rd Round:​
 This was essentially the offer release round. One HR panelist was present. He 
asked about my family background and future plans, then congratulated me and 
shared the offer details.​
 
Overall Experience:​
 All three panels were extremely friendly and made me feel at ease from the beginning. 
The interviews felt more like interactive discussions than formal assessments. The 
interviewers even guided me during the process whenever I needed help. 
Tips for Interviews: 
●​ Be thorough with your projects and core technical subjects.​
 
●​ Practice explaining your projects clearly and confidently.​
 
●​ Stay calm and treat the interview like a conversation.​
 
●​ Be honest if you don't know something—interviewers appreciate honesty and 
clarity.

Job Title: Data Engineer 
Organization: TICMPL Software Business Unit - Part of the Murugappa Group 
Location: Guindy, Chennai 
Job Summary: 
TICMPL is seeking a talented Data Engineer to join our team in Chennai. In this role, you 
will design and implement robust data pipelines to process telematics IOT streaming 
data in the cloud. Your work will play a crucial role in generating insights and process 
the streaming data that drive business decisions in areas such as vehicle behaviour 
analysis, fleet management, predictive maintenance, and diagnostics 
As a Data Engineer at TICMPL, you will be at the forefront of data innovation, 
optimizing the cloud resources, Run the ETL processes and transform the data for use 
by Data scientist and Applications. Join us and play a key role in transforming how we 
use data to drive insights and value!  
Key Responsibilities: 
·         Data Pipeline Design: Architect and implement scalable cloud-based data pipelines 
for processing telematics data 
·         Data Processing: Develop and maintain efficient data processing systems to meet 
business requirements 
·         Visualization Support: Assist data analysts in creating impactful visualizations to 
help stakeholders interpret data effectively 
·         Data Quality Assurance: Ensure the accuracy and reliability of data throughout the 
651 

 
pipeline 
·         Optimization: Continuously optimize data processing systems for performance and 
scalability 
  
Key skills required: 
·         Cloud & Database Technologies:  Experience with cloud-native data processing 
tools (e.g., GCP Dataflow, Data Fusion, Dataproc) & Proficiency in database systems 
like MongoDB and MySQL. 
·         Big Data Expertise: Familiarity with Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, and KSQL. 
·         ETL Development: Experience in building and maintaining ETL pipelines using 
cloud-native or open-source tools 
·         Data Modelling & Integration: Familiarity with data modelling techniques, data 
integration strategies, and best practices in data governance 
·         Data Visualization: Experience with tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker. 
·         Programming: Strong skills in Python or Java. 
·         Problem Solving & Attention to Detail: Ability to diagnose and resolve complex 
data-related issues efficiently. 
·         Communication & Collaboration: Excellent interpersonal skills to work effectively 
with cross-functional teams. 
  
Preferred Experience 
·         Proven track record of working with complex data sets. 
·         Familiarity with data modelling, integration, and maintaining data quality. 
·         Strong focus on innovation and objective thinking
entries.preparationMaterials:
I used ChatGPT and books related to Machine Learning for theory preparation. For DSA,

entries.suggestions:
1.​ For technical tests, start preparing from August. Solve DSA problems (even if 
not required) and practice quantitative aptitude questions. Time management is 
key—anyone can solve these questions if given enough time, so the important 
factor is speed. Sometimes, you need to outperform others by being faster. 
Practice well and make use of the mock tests provided by the placement team. 
653 

 
Learning ML, AI, Data Science, or Data Analytics can also be an added 
advantage.​
 
2.​ For case studies, I suggest having peripheral knowledge about everything. This 
can be developed by reading about the job role, the company, the market, and 
how they function.​
 
3.​ GD :(There was no GD for my company, but I would like to share what went 
wrong with another shortlist I received.) Group discussions usually involve 8–10 
students and can be conducted online or offline. A key point is to avoid staying in 
the background—try to take the lead. However, don’t lead by dominating others. 
Be respectful and give everyone a fair chance to speak. Aim to act as both a 
contributor and a moderator.​
 
4.​ Interview : There were two rounds, one technical and one HR. The technical 
panel consisted of three people. It was a bit difficult for me as I was asked two 
technical questions to assess my problem-solving skills, which were not easy for 
a first-timer. However, I stayed calm and composed. The interviewers were polite 
and respectful and gave me enough time to respond, which helped me solve the 
problems. A better approach would be to practice sample problems relevant to 
the specific job role. They also asked about my resume in detail—from A to Z. 
Being confident about everything mentioned in your resume creates a strong 
impression.​
 In the HR round, be honest—that’s all I would say.

Technical/HR Tests: 
The online assessment (OA) consisted of basic aptitude and DSA-based questions. 
●​ Difficulty: Easy 
●​ Duration: 1 hour 30 minutes 
●​ Tips: Regular practice of easy to medium-level questions on LeetCode and 
GeeksforGeeks (GFG) is helpful. Focus on coding in your preferred language 
(C++, Java, or Python) and develop strong fundamentals, including OOPs 
concepts and basic math/reasoning skills. 
 
Interviews: 
The process included three rounds in total — two technical and one HR. 
 
Technical Round 1: 
664 

 
Focused on DSA problems (including topics like arrays and dynamic 
programming), sometimes discussed on pen and paper. 
In some cases, candidates were given coding tasks involving constraints (e.g., solving 
without STL) and were asked to explain their approaches. 
●​ Duration: 30–60 minutes 
●​ Difficulty: Medium 
 
Technical Round 2: 
Covered a range of topics including OOPs concepts, statistics-related questions, 
and puzzles. 
In some instances, candidates were asked resume-based questions or to implement 
basic algorithms like Merge Sort. 
●​ Duration: 10–30 minutes (varied by candidate) 
●​ Difficulty: Medium to Hard 
 
HR Round: 
The HR round was generally light and conversational. Topics included personal 
background, relocation preferences, hobbies, strengths, and general fit. 
●​ Duration: 5–20 minutes 
●​ Difficulty: Easy 
●​ Tips: Be confident, honest, and show flexibility — especially for location and 
work expectations. 
 
Additional Notes: 
Candidates are advised to go through their resumes thoroughly, brush up on 
DSA daily, and be well-prepared with core programming concepts in their chosen 
language. Interviewers may test adaptability in problem-solving, such as solving the 
same problem using different methods or without using built-in data structures.

consistent habit of DSA practice is crucial—aim to solve 2–3 problems daily on 
platforms like LeetCode and Codeforces. This regularity builds problem-solving

for clarity and impact. 
Don't overlook aptitude and core subject preparation, especially for Online 
Assessments. For students from core branches (like Civil), consider balancing your GPA 
by taking relatively easier electives like GN.

code without heavy reliance on STL. During the HR round, stay calm, be confident, and 
express genuine interest in the company. Show flexibility toward relocation and 
in-office roles. 
Finally, actively network with seniors and seek guidance throughout the process. If 
you're targeting SDE or analytics roles, develop a daily DSA habit by the end of 5th 
semester and simultaneously work on building additional skills such as development or 
machine learning.

entries.testAndInterview:
1) Technical/HR Tests:​
 The technical test was conducted on the HackerRank platform and lasted 
approximately 2 hours and 30 minutes to 3 hours. It consisted of three Data 
Structures and Algorithms (DSA) problems, with difficulty levels ranging from 
medium to hard. The questions covered topics such as Dynamic Programming, 
Huffman Coding, and Graphs involving queries. One of the graph-based 
questions was particularly lengthy and challenging. It was not mandatory to 
solve all three problems to qualify; solving two was generally sufficient. 
Tips for Preparation: 
●​ Focus on mastering DSA concepts through consistent practice. 
●​ Practice on competitive coding platforms like HackerRank, LeetCode, or 
Codeforces. 
●​ Understand the logic behind each algorithm rather than just memorizing 
the code. 
2) Interviews:​
 There were two interview rounds: a Technical Interview and an HR Interview, 
both conducted online. 
695 

 
●​ Technical Interview (Duration: ~1 hour):​
 The round began with a self-introduction and then moved on to questions 
from DSA, SQL, and Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs). The 
interviewer asked for a pseudo-code explanation of a project mentioned in 
the resume and also discussed the candidate's entire resume in detail. 
Additionally, a puzzle (the King and Wine Bottle puzzle) was asked. 
○​ Difficulty Level: Easy to moderate 
○​ Interviewer Attitude: Friendly and supportive; provided hints when 
the candidate was stuck.​
 
●​ HR Interview (Duration: ~30 minutes):​
 This round was focused on behavioral and personality-based questions. 
The interviewer reviewed the resume thoroughly and asked about hobbies, 
co-curricular activities, and interests. There was also a strong focus on 
internships and project work. Having relevant project and internship 
experience proved to be advantageous. 
○​ Difficulty Level: Easy 
○​ Interviewer Attitude: Friendly and engaging

Start preparing early—at least 5 to 6 months in advance—and stay consistent. 
Aim to complete most of your preparation before September so you can focus on 
revision once placements begin.

Consider giving mock interviews to build confidence. 
Actively contribute to your projects, even if others don’t. You’ll learn a lot by 
simply engaging sincerely. Choose your courses wisely and pay attention in 
class—they often add value during placements.

Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) concepts using coursework materials.

requirements. Use mock interviews extensively to improve technical communication 
and confidence. Be thoroughly familiar with every detail on your resume, stay calm 
during interviews, and avoid imposter syndrome—confidence and clear communication 
can make a significant difference in your performance.

Selection Process: Resume Shortlist → 3 Group Discussion (GD) Rounds → CEO 
Interaction. There was no online test. The GDs covered both general strategy topics 
and Ola-specific business cases, with interviewers asking cross-questions and 
challenging participants to justify their arguments. The first two GDs were online, the 
final GD and CEO interaction were offline. The final discussion panel consisted of 
multiple interviewers, while the CEO round focused on the resume, problem-solving 
ability, and overall fit. The process emphasized structured thinking, logical reasoning, 
confidence, and clear communication over technical knowledge.

tools to improve formatting and structure. Since there was no online test, preparation 
focused on GDs by using LLMs for company research, studying Ola's recent businesses 
and ventures, and practicing with case competition books to build structured discussion 
frameworks.
entries.suggestions:
Develop strong case-solving and structured thinking skills, research the company's 
business and culture thoroughly, and practice defending your ideas with logical 
reasoning. Speak confidently, communicate your thought process clearly, and don't 
hesitate to admit when you don't know something. Strategic preparation, self-belief, 
and confidence throughout the interview process can make a significant difference.

medium/hard problems and Brainstellar-style puzzles. Round 2 (1-1.5 hours) is a

shortlisting filter across most roles, so consistent practice pays off. A CGPA of 8 and

profiles demanding more. Staying calm and confident through the process makes a real 
difference.

work/college experience. DSA knowledge isn't strictly required.

entries.testAndInterview:
Technical / HR Tests:​
There were no tests for this profile. The company evaluated candidates directly 
through the resume and the interview.​
 
Interview Experience:​
The interview was mostly HR-focused and culture-fit oriented, with only a small 
amount of technical discussion. It lasted around 35–40 minutes. The difficulty level 
was easy to moderate. They asked only a few technical questions, mainly centered 
around the projects I had done.​
The interview was conducted online by a Japanese panel consisting of two members.​
The main areas they focused on were my ability to adjust to Japanese culture, my 
motivation for working in Japan, my openness to learning Japanese, my general 
attitude and flexibility, and how clearly I could explain my projects.​
 

337 
During the interview, they also took time to explain the company’s structure, the 
different domains they work in, and the flexibility offered in choosing work areas.​
One advantage I had was that I had completed the Japanese-I (ED1091) course. I also 
took help from the course professor for interview resources and prepared basic 
Japanese interview etiquette.​
My tips for this interview would be: learn simple Japanese greetings and a 
self-introduction, show genuine interest in working in Japan, express clearly that you 
are willing to learn and adapt, keep your project explanations concise, and maintain a 
polite and calm attitude because Japanese interviews value humility and consistency.​
Case Study / Additional Rounds:​
There were no case studies or extra rounds for this role.​
Group Discussion:​
There was no GD round for this company.​
The interview was easy to moderate in difficulty and mainly focused on HR and 
culture-fit questions, with only light technical discussion around my projects. The 
interviewers were very polite, patient, and encouraging, which made the conversation 
comfortable. There were two interviewers on the panel, both from Japan. The entire 
process had only one round, and it was conducted online. Based on my experience, the 
most useful tips are to learn basic Japanese greetings and a short self-introduction, be 
genuinely open to learning and adapting to Japanese work culture, keep project 
explanations clear and concise, and maintain a calm, respectful attitude throughout the 
interview.

There were approximately 16 subjective questions, divided into four sections: statistics, 
probability, distributions, and mathematical aptitude. The allotted time was 
approximately 60 minutes. Additionally, there was a psychometric test, which should 
be taken seriously.​
​
Difficulty: Moderate to easy.​
​
The interviewers were very friendly and supportive, providing guidance whenever I got 
stuck. There were two rounds in total.​
​
The first round was a technical interview with two panel members, followed by a 
managerial/behavioural round. Questions were primarily based on the projects 
mentioned in my resume, with the interviewers going deeper into the underlying 
concepts. A thorough understanding of bagging and boosting models was tested. A 
basic understanding of finance concepts such as volatility, Sharpe ratio, and hedging 
instruments is an added advantage.​
​
One basic puzzle was asked, along with a follow-up question. 
​
The behavioural round consisted of standard HR questions.

entries.suggestions:

mentioned in your resume and be able to explain all your projects clearly.​

advantage. Familiarize yourself with financial metrics such as the Sharpe ratio, 
maximum drawdown, and other related concepts. Additionally, develop a basic 
understanding of hedging strategies.​

Practice puzzles from the Green Book. It is also recommended to include projects that 
combine both machine learning and finance.​
​
Do not take the psychometric test lightly.​

technical-motivational questions.​
​
HR Round (30 min): General behavioural questions.

Questions were basic reasoning type (missing numbers, patterns, etc), basic probability 
type questions and one coding question. ​
I would say the difficulty level was hard when it came to cases as the interviewers 
were not supportive during the case, I had to assume or did guestimation for most of 
my values, minimum to no data was provided.​
​
When it comes to other technical questions, I would say the questions were easy- 
basic sql questions, pandas questions, questions related to my resume if they find 
 

458 
anything relevant. ​

1 panelist in each round, simple tip is to be real and honest and they will test you on 
your area of expertise as they tested me through case round and not through coding as 
I clearly denied that I don't know coding much, other than that try to keep up the 
energy during interview even if the interviewer is trying to demotivate you. ​
​
2 rounds, both offline and one after the other.

entries.testAndInterview:
Tests: 
There were approximately 16 subjective questions. It consisted of 4 sections - 
statistics, probability, distributions, and some mathematical aptitude. 60 minutes 
approx time was given. One more Psychometric test. Psychometric tests must be taken 
seriously.​
 
Interview: 
Difficulty: Moderate/easy​
The interviewers were very friendly and helped me if I got stuck. There were two 
rounds.​
The first round was Technical with 2 panelists and the last round was 
Managerial/behavioral.​
Questions Were Asked Only from my resume projects and then the interviewer went a 
little deeper into the concepts. Understanding of bagging and boosting models were 
 

468 
tested thoroughly. Basic understanding of Finance such as volatility, sharpe ratio, 
hedging instruments is a plus.​
One basic puzzle was asked and a follow up.​
For the behavioral round they asked a standard HR question.

entries.suggestions:
Be thorough with your resume first and foremost. Should know each and every line in 
your resume and be able to explain all the projects clearly.  Understanding of 
application of ML models on financial data is good to have. Read about Financial 
Metrics such as Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown etc. and get a basic understanding 
of hedging strategies. Practice puzzles from book.​
I would recommend putting projects that combine both ML and finance.​
Please do not take the psychometric test lightly.
